subject: Netherlands

claims.text: The Netherlands is geographically very low relative to sea level, with about 26% of its area and 21% of its population below sea level.
Netherlands literally means lower countries, in reference to its low elevation and flat topography.
Most of the areas below sea level, known as polders, are the result of land reclamation that began in the 14th century.
A polder usually has an excess of water, which is pumped out or drained by opening sluices at low tide.
A polder is a low-lying tract of land enclosed by embankments known as dikes, and is at risk of flooding at all times.
